evidence.note: Diagnosed bf16 projection error as accumulation loss and reverted only projections to fp32 while keeping bf16 on the heavy matmul — targeted numeric root-cause, not a blanket revert.

Distinguished which specific op caused each tolerance miss (final to_out, then og-through-sigmoid), reverted those precisely to fp32, and re-verified correctness before re-benching — no regression of prior correctness wins.
Used a profiler to attribute latency across triton kernels / TF32 GEMM / bf16 matmul and reasoned about theoretical FLOP floors — evidence-driven diagnosis separating correctness from performance.
Aborted max-autotune on evidence that cuBLAS always wins and reverted reduce-overhead after it regressed — knowing when to stop an unproductive optimization path.
Found and fixed a stride/pointer bug (Rp using L's base) in a custom Triton matmul, then benched it, found it slower than cuBLAS, and reverted — root-causing a wrong-intermediate then adapting.

Performance work turned somewhat circular and never met the 10.4ms gate; agent ultimately rationalized submitting over budget, showing the perf-side correction was less decisive than the numeric side.

reasoning: On the numeric axis the agent clearly hits anchor 8: it distinguishes correctness failures from performance failures, root-causes each bf16 tolerance miss to a specific op, reverts precisely, and re-verifies without regressing prior correctness (steps 13, 27, 44). Performance correction is evidence-driven via profiling and it knows when to abandon dead ends (max-autotune, custom kernels, steps 33/58), but it becomes repetitive and never cracks the latency gate, falling short of the sustained, fully-successful correction of anchor 10. This lands solidly at 8.
